name: Telegram
tagline: Free cloud messaging app with channels, large group chats, and a public bot platform.
description: Telegram is a free cloud messaging app with channel broadcasting, large group chats, and a public bot platform for automated services.
pros: History lives in the vendor cloud and follows a user between devices without manual transfer
Channels let one administrator publish to a subscriber audience without per-member licensing
A public bot platform puts notifications and tools inside the chat window where people already are
The core application carries no per-seat charge, which this dataset records simply as Free
This repository’s nonprofit guidance recommends free Telegram groups for keeping volunteers informed
cons: Accounts are personal rather than organizational, so member onboarding and offboarding stay manual
Cloud storage by default leaves no on-premises or region-locked deployment option for regulated data
No certifications, retention policies, or admin audit logs are recorded here, so governance must be verified with the vendor

features.name: Cloud-synced message history
features.description: Conversations are stored on the vendor’s servers and restored on any device the account signs into. The dataset records cloud as the deployment model.

features.name: Channels for broadcasts
features.description: Publish-only spaces where administrators post and subscribers receive; member lists stay hidden from the audience.

features.name: Groups with admin controls
features.description: Conversational rooms with administrators who hold moderation and membership permissions. Permission tiers are not itemized in this dataset.

features.name: Public bot platform
features.description: A public API lets developers register bots that answer in chats and post to channels, turning the app into a surface for automated services.

features.name: Cross-device sessions
features.description: The same account runs on phone, desktop, and web at once, with conversation state carried between them.

features.name: File and media sharing
features.description: Photos, documents, and other files pass between members inside a conversation. Size limits are not recorded in this dataset.

features.name: Secret chats option
features.description: An opt-in mode that keeps a conversation on one device pair for end-to-end encryption instead of syncing it through the cloud.

features.name: Chat folders and search
features.description: Users group conversations into folders and search history to find a message without scrolling. Folder behavior is not detailed in this dataset.

content.title: Messaging with history in the cloud
content.body: Telegram is a consumer messaging application, not a business phone system: there are no numbers to provision, no seats to license, and no PBX anywhere in the product. Message history is stored in the vendor’s cloud and syncs across a user’s devices, so installing the app on a new phone restores conversations instead of stranding them. Our dataset files Telegram under Communication as a free product, with a recorded price range of Free and an overall score of 4.4/5 across 720 reviews. Nothing here depends on an account being opened; the description follows what the product is documented to be.

content.title: Channels, groups, and broadcasts
content.body: Two mechanics carry most of Telegram’s public life. Groups are conversational: members talk to each other, administrators hold moderation and membership controls, and topics keep threads separated inside a busy room. Channels are publish-only: an administrator posts, subscribers receive, and the audience list stays invisible to the members. That asymmetry is what makes channels usable for announcements at a scale where a group would bury the announcement under replies. Both are created instantly by any account, with no organizational approval step and no per-member license attached.

content.title: The bot platform
content.body: Telegram exposes a public Bot API, so any developer can register a bot that answers inside chats, pushes channel posts, or runs inline lookups without shipping a separate application. That turns the messenger into a distribution surface: notifications, forms, search tools, and small storefronts all live in the same window where the conversation already happens. This repository records that an API is available for Telegram but does not catalog specific bots or third-party services, so what exists beyond the platform itself should be explored through the vendor’s developer documentation rather than inferred from this page.

content.title: Cloud chats, secret chats, and what that means
content.body: The default Telegram conversation is a cloud chat: content lives on the vendor’s servers, which is exactly why it syncs between devices. An optional secret chat mode keeps a conversation on a single device pair for end-to-end encryption, at the cost of losing that history when the device changes. The split is the honest answer to a privacy question — convenience by default, a stricter mode by choice. Neither certifications, admin audit logs, nor data-residency terms for Telegram appear anywhere in this repository, so organizations with formal requirements should verify current documentation with the vendor rather than infer anything from the app’s reputation.

content.title: What Telegram costs
content.body: Cost, on this record, is zero. Our dataset gives Telegram a price range of Free with no paid pricing model in these fields — no per-seat charge, no plan tier, and no metered usage for the core application. What the record does not capture is how the service is funded or whether commercial terms exist for organizational use — questions a buyer should raise directly with the vendor. Telegram is rarely chosen or rejected on price; administration, retention control, and whether a consumer-shaped tool can carry a business workload decide it. Nothing on this page was produced by operating a Telegram account — it reflects the vendor’s published documentation and this repository’s stored fields.

content.title: Where teams actually use Telegram
content.body: This repository’s own content places Telegram in volunteer and community settings rather than in enterprise directories: a nonprofit hub here recommends free Telegram groups for keeping volunteers informed about upcoming opportunities and last-minute changes. The situations below match how the product is actually adopted rather than how a communications suite is sold.
items: Volunteer and community groups that need to reach people without buying licenses
One-way announcement channels for a club, an open project, or a local community
Cross-device personal messaging where history must follow the user between phones
Bot-driven notifications and lookups delivered inside a chat window
Small organizations that want structured messaging before investing in a phone system

content.title: Where Telegram stops
content.body: Telegram is organized around personal accounts rather than company directories, so onboarding and offboarding members is manual and there is no seat-level control plane for an IT team to own. Cloud-stored history means content sits with the vendor by default, and organizations that need region-locked or on-premises storage have no deployment option here. The absence of recorded certifications, retention policies, and admin audit capability in this repository compounds that governance gap: a compliance team reading these fields starts from nothing. The free price removes budget friction but answers none of those questions.

content.title: Telegram’s position in this dataset
content.body: In this dataset Telegram is measured against RingCentral, Dialpad, and Vonage — all paid, business-shaped products — as well as Slack, Zoom, and Microsoft Teams. The comparison is nearly categorical: those tools buy administration, support contracts, and enterprise packaging, while Telegram offers a free, fast messenger with channels and bots and no organizational layer at all. Our dataset carries an overall score of 4.4/5 for Telegram across 720 recorded reviews. The verdict is narrow: it fits communities, volunteer groups, and small teams that value free, cloud-synced messaging, and it stops where a company needs directories, audit trails, and contracted support.

faqs.question: Is Telegram free for organizations too?
faqs.answer: This dataset records Telegram’s price range as Free with no paid plan in these fields. Commercial or support terms for organizational use are not recorded here, so confirm them with the vendor.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a Telegram group and a channel?
faqs.answer: Groups are conversational — members reply to each other under administrator controls. Channels are publish-only: admins post and subscribers receive, with the member list hidden from the audience.

faqs.question: What can bots do inside Telegram?
faqs.answer: Telegram exposes a public Bot API, so developers can build chat assistants, notifications, and inline tools that run inside conversations and channels. This repository does not catalog specific bots.

faqs.question: Are Telegram messages stored in the cloud?
faqs.answer: Yes, by default. Cloud chats sync across a user’s devices through the vendor’s servers; an optional secret chat mode stays on one device pair instead and does not sync between them.

faqs.question: Can Telegram replace a business phone system?
faqs.answer: No. Telegram has no numbers, dialer, call routing, or contact center capability. For calling, this dataset points to products such as RingCentral or Dialpad; Telegram covers messaging, channels, and bots.

author: Emily Nakamura
learningCurve: Messaging, groups, and channels are immediate; the bot platform and the admin permission model are where time goes.
whoShouldUse: Communities, volunteer groups, creators, and small teams that want free messaging with channel-style announcements, cross-device history, and simple bot automation.
whoShouldNotUse: Organizations needing a business phone system, companies that require seat-level administration or audit logs, and buyers who need compliance certifications this repository does not record.
